accessibility.title: Accessibility
accessibility.intro: This page reports how accessible the E-Portfolio Hochschule Bremen was at the time of the last audit: what was tested, with which tools, and what remains open.
accessibility.notFormal: This is not a formal declaration under the German accessibility regulation (BITV). The application is a prototype from a bachelor thesis; there is no body that could take responsibility for a conformance claim, and no monitoring or arbitration process. What is reported here is an audit result, not a promise.

status.title: Audit status
status.result: 36 pages with content of their own tested, in light and in dark mode, 73 runs in total. Two departures from the simple arithmetic: the help page runs twice per mode, because it shows different things without a session and as an administrator, and the page “create project” creates a draft when opened and therefore runs only once per test run. No remaining level A or AA violation outside the limits listed below.

method.title: Method
method.intro: Testing runs automatically against the built application, not against the development build. Each page goes through five checks, in light and in dark mode:
items: Rule check with axe-core against WCAG 2.0 A and AA, WCAG 2.1 AA and WCAG 2.2 AA.
Heading structure: exactly one top-level heading per page, no skipped level.

Keyboard walkthrough: the page is actually tabbed through. The check confirms that focus finds its way out again, that every tab stop is visible, and that every control meant to be a tab stop can be reached.
Focus visibility: where comparing computed styles is not enough, an image comparison of the same area with and without focus decides.
Narrow screens: at 320 CSS pixels the page itself must not scroll sideways. Wide content scrolls within its own area.

scope.title: Pages covered
scope.intro: The audit covers every page of the application:
items: the public views: home, project library, project details, public portfolios, contact and support, help and documentation, this page, the error page and the no-access notice,
sign-in, the four-step registration and the password pages,
the signed-in views: own portfolio, edit profile, create project and project metadata,
the editorial views: own reviews and review mode,
the administration area with dashboard, projects, accounts, categories, semesters, study structure, top 10 management including its audit log, support requests and home page texts,
the block-based editor as a whole.

limits.title: Known limits
limits.intro: The following points are known and not fixed. They are listed because an unsupported claim would be worse than a stated gap:
items: There is no imprint and no privacy policy yet. Both addresses lead to a placeholder page; the audit covers them, but what is tested there is the placeholder and not any content.

No walkthrough with screen reader software. Structure, labels, roles and status regions were checked in the code and automatically; a run with an actual screen reader is still outstanding. An automated test finds only part of the problems and does not replace it.

Videos and audio have no subtitle track and no transcripts (success criteria 1.2.1 and 1.2.2). The data model has no field for them; the existing “caption” attribute is a caption below the media, not a subtitle track.

The content of embedded third-party media comes from the respective providers (YouTube, Vimeo, Figma, CodePen). It is neither tested nor under our control; the YouTube player brings violations of its own. What is tested is the embed itself, meaning its title and its label.

In the contributor groups on project cards the pictures overlap. A covered picture therefore offers a smaller area at rest than the required 24 by 24 pixels (success criterion 2.5.8). With a mouse or the keyboard the group fans out before the click and the area is sufficient; on touch screens there is no hover, and the area stays too small.
An interrupted file upload cannot be resumed, only restarted.
When printing a project, the browser decides where pages break. Where exactly that happens is therefore not predictable.

What is tested is the initial state of each page. Anything that appears only behind an opened dialog, a dropdown menu or in the middle of a multi-step flow is covered by the test case of the respective ticket, not by this audit.

Links to external sites lead to content beyond the operator's control. No violation was apparent when the link was set; there is no continuous review without a concrete reason.

related.title: Related pages
related.intro: How this portal handles personal data and how accessible it is are each covered on a page of their own:

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: Which personal data this portal processes, what for, who besides the operator gets to see it, and what rights you have.
privacy.prototypeNote: The application is a prototype from a bachelor thesis and is operated privately, not by Hochschule Bremen. It is not a permanently operated service; when it is shut down depends on how the thesis proceeds.

controller.title: Controller
controller.intro: The controller within the meaning of the General Data Protection Regulation is:
controller.noDpo: No data protection officer has been appointed. The conditions of Article 37 GDPR are not met for a privately operated prototype of this size.
controller.missing: This build of the application carries no controller details. They are set from the environment at build time and are therefore absent from a development build. A publicly reachable build without them is a mistake, not a choice.

data.title: What data is processed
data.intro: What is collected is what the application needs in order to work:
items: Account: first and last name, your private email address, your university email address, your password as an irreversible hash, role and account status, the state of both address verifications, and a note on whether the password must be changed. The password hash leaves the server in no response. Your university address is seen only by you and by the administration in user management; it is never delivered to other accounts.

Public profile: your name, your private email address, your biography and your profile picture can be retrieved through your portfolio page without signing in, as soon as the account exists. The address appears there as a way to contact the author. That also means a harvester can pick it up; it is a decision made by this portal and not a choice you get to make.

Projects: title, summary, content blocks, tags and the assignment to faculty, degree programme, degree and semester. A draft is seen only by you, by the project members you entered, and by the administration; after submission also by the editor in charge. Once published, a project can be read by anyone.
Status history: for every step a project takes, who triggered it and when. It reveals how often a piece of work was sent back for revision.
Editorial notes: an editor can attach remarks to a project that are marked internal and are not visible to students. They concern you and form part of an access request under Article 15 GDPR.
Uploaded files: images, video, audio and documents, each with file name, size, type and the account that uploaded them.
Comments and reactions on projects, each with the account they come from. On a published project the comment list can be read without signing in; your name then appears publicly beneath it.

Enquiries through the public contact form: name, email address, category, subject and the free text of the message. If you were signed in when sending, your account is recorded as well, even though that record appears in no view. It is also recorded which administration account handled the enquiry and when.
Verification codes for your two addresses, until they are redeemed or expire.
Technical access data: IP address, time, requested address and browser identification. These arise in the operation of any web server and appear in its log.

Failed attempts: to fend off bulk attempts, the server counts unsuccessful tries separately by email address and by IP address, at sign-in, at both verification steps, when resetting a password, and at the contact form. The counters live in memory only, expire with their time window, and are empty after the server restarts; they never reach the database.
For editorial and administration accounts additionally: nominations for the home page, the audit trail of the top ten selection, and a note on who currently holds an editing lock.

purposes.title: Purposes and legal bases
items: Keeping an account, signing in and resetting passwords: performance of the usage relationship and pre-contractual steps, Article 6(1)(b) GDPR.

Writing, submitting, reviewing and publishing projects: performance of the usage relationship, Article 6(1)(b) GDPR. When a project becomes public is your decision when you submit it; your profile, by contrast, can be retrieved publicly from the moment the account is created.

Deriving the role from the university address: at registration, the domain of your university address alone decides whether the account is kept as a student or a staff account; if it matches neither of the two configured lists, registration is refused and no account is created. This happens without human involvement. Article 6(1)(b) GDPR.
Verifying both addresses in order to limit access to members of the university: legitimate interest, Article 6(1)(f) GDPR.
Answering enquiries from the contact form: legitimate interest, Article 6(1)(f) GDPR.
Keeping logs and counting failed attempts in order to protect operation against abuse: legitimate interest, Article 6(1)(f) GDPR.

processors.title: Recipients and processors
processors.intro: The application does not run on hardware of its own. Three service providers carry the operation; on top of them come the providers of embedded media, as soon as a project contains any:
items: Server operation: Hostinger International Ltd., Lithuania. The application and its database run on a virtual server of this provider; the data centre is located in Germany.

File storage: Microsoft Azure Blob Storage, provided within the European Union by Microsoft Ireland Operations Ltd., Ireland. Uploaded images, video, audio and documents are held in a private storage account in the Sweden Central region, that is, in Sweden. The store permits no anonymous access; files are delivered by the application alone.
Mail delivery: an SMTP relay operated by Hostinger International Ltd., Lithuania. Verification, notification and password messages go out through it. The connection to it is encrypted (STARTTLS).

Embedded media: if a published project contains a video or embed block, your browser loads that content directly from YouTube (Google Ireland Ltd. and Google LLC, United States), Vimeo (Vimeo.com Inc., United States), Figma (Figma Inc., United States) or CodePen (CodePen Inc., United States). Those providers thereby learn your IP address, your browser identification and the page you opened, and they can access information stored on your device. This happens as the page is built, not only when you press play.
processors.note: Server operation, file storage and mail delivery are within the European Union. For file storage, a Microsoft sub-processor may access data from a third country; the provider's standard contractual clauses apply to that. The providers of embedded media, by contrast, are based in the United States, and the data named in the last point flows there. There are no further recipients.

retention.title: Retention
items: Account, profile and projects remain for as long as the account exists.

You can neither withdraw nor delete a published project yourself. Only an editor or the administration can take it out of the published state, and you can delete a project of your own only while it is still a draft. For anything beyond that, the manual route in the next section applies.

Enquiries from the contact form remain until they have been dealt with and are deleted on request afterwards. The reply itself is written by the administration from its own mailbox; that correspondence then lives there and no longer in this system.
Verification codes expire 24 hours after they are issued.
The server logs roll over by size: at most five files of ten megabytes each per service, with older entries overwritten in the process.
The counters of failed attempts expire with their time window and are empty after the server restarts.

deletion.title: Deleting an account
deletion.text: Here the prototype is candid about itself: there is no button with which you can delete your own account. The administration can deactivate an account, after which it can no longer sign in; the row in the database remains so that the attribution of already published projects does not fall apart. Actual erasure within the meaning of Article 17 GDPR is therefore done by hand: write to the address above and the account, profile, projects and uploaded files will be removed.

rights.title: Your rights
rights.intro: In relation to the controller named above you have the right to:
items: Access to the data processed about you, Article 15 GDPR. This also covers what the interface does not show you, such as editorial notes and the status history of your projects.
Rectification of inaccurate data, Article 16 GDPR.
Erasure, Article 17 GDPR, by the route described in the previous section.
Restriction of processing, Article 18 GDPR.
Data portability, Article 20 GDPR.
Objection to processing based on a legitimate interest, Article 21 GDPR.
rights.authority: Independently of this, you may lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority under Article 77 GDPR. The competent authority is the one of your habitual residence, your place of work, or the place of the alleged infringement.

contactForm.title: If you only used the contact form
contactForm.text: The contact form is open without signing in. Whoever uses it leaves a name, an email address, a category, a subject and the text of the message, but has no account and therefore no route through the interface to view that data or have it deleted. For this case an informal message to the address above is enough: state the email address you wrote from and roughly when. The enquiry will then be looked up, quoted back to you on request, and deleted.

noTracking.title: No tracking, no consent banner
noTracking.text: The portal itself uses no analytics and no advertising services, measures no behaviour, and loads neither fonts nor maps from third parties. Everything the interface needs comes from its own server. There is no profiling.
noTracking.consent: The one exception is the embedded media described under “Recipients”. They appear on a page because an author placed them in a project, and they load from their providers' servers as soon as the page is built. The cleaner approach would be to load them only after consent. This prototype does not do that; it is a known limitation, and it is named here rather than covered up with a banner that controls nothing.
noTracking.storage: Stored in your browser are: your signed-in session, that is the sign-in token, its expiry and the details of your account (name, both addresses, role and status); during a registration in progress, your two addresses and the state of verification; the path to return to after signing in; and your choice between light and dark mode. All of it stays on your device and goes to nobody else.
noTracking.logout: Signing out deletes the sign-in token from your browser. On the server it stays valid until its expiry: the API keeps no session that it could end. That, too, is a deliberately documented limitation of this prototype.

indexing.title: Not findable through search engines
indexing.text: Public project and portfolio pages carry real names. So that they do not become findable through search engines, this portal explicitly instructs that every one of its pages and every file it delivers must not be taken into an index and that no link from it be followed. Crawling is deliberately left permitted, because a search engine can only obey that instruction if it is allowed to read it. The portal is therefore reachable by anyone who knows its address, and not through a search for your name.

help.title: Help & documentation
help.intro: How to use the e-portfolio: find and read published work, write and submit your own projects, review them editorially and administer the platform.
help.roleHint: This page shows the sections that match your access. Without signing in you see what is possible without an account; a signed-in account also sees the editor, an editor also sees the review section, an administrator sees everything.
help.imageNote: The figures are captured from the running application with sample data. They show the English interface in light mode, even if you are currently using German or dark mode; layout and controls are the same.

feedback.text: If a question remains open or something does not work, you can reach the administration team through the contact form:

visitors.title: Exploring the portal
visitors.intro: Anyone can read published work, with or without an account. An account is only needed to write something yourself.

browse.title: Finding and filtering projects
browse.text: The entry “Projects” lists every published student work. The search field covers title, summary, the author's name and the tags; it does not match the names of project members. The filter column on the left narrows the list further.
steps: Six filter groups: faculty, degree programme, degree, semester, project type and category. Each group accepts several values at once.
Search, filters and page number live in the address. A result can therefore be shared, and the browser's back button returns to the previous selection.
Above the list you see how many works the current selection matches.
browse.imageAlt: The page “Student projects”: on the left the filter column with the group “Faculty/institution” expanded into five checkboxes, on the right the search field, the result count and project cards showing cover image, faculty code, project type, summary, semester and reaction count.

projectPage.title: Reading a project page
projectPage.text: The detail page shows the work as its author laid it out: cover image, title, summary and below them the content blocks. There are fifteen kinds: heading, paragraph, list, quote, source code, divider, table, image, gallery, video, audio, document, embed, formula and table of contents.
steps: Beside the content you find the details of the work: degree programme, semester, category, subject and the people involved.
The hand below the content is the reaction, the counterpart of applause. It is open to signed-in accounts and can be taken back.
The printer icon on the cover image produces a PDF version through the browser's print dialogue.
projectPage.imageAlt: The detail view of a published work: a large cover image with a printer icon, below it title, summary and the content; on the right a column with the details of the work.
projectPage.imageCaption: Detail view of a published work.

top10.title: The top 10 of the year
top10.text: Below the opening section of the home page sits the curated top 10 list. Editors propose works for it; the administration decides on inclusion and order.
steps: The order is chosen, not calculated: it reflects neither click counts nor reactions.
Every place links to the project page of the work.
top10.imageAlt: The “Top 10” section of the home page: a heading, an explanatory sentence and below them cards of the selected works with place number and cover image.
top10.imageCaption: The top 10 list on the home page.

portfolio.title: Someone's portfolio
portfolio.text: The name attached to a work leads to that person's public portfolio: a short introduction and all of their published work on one page.
steps: Only published work is visible. Drafts and submitted contributions stay hidden.
A person's university address never appears in public. The private address, on the other hand, is part of the public profile and is therefore visible without signing in.
portfolio.imageAlt: The public portfolio of a student: a profile header with initials, name, role badge and short introduction, below it the cards of the published works.
portfolio.imageCaption: The public portfolio of a person.

account.title: Creating an account and signing in
account.text: A portfolio of your own needs an account. Registration takes three steps and requires an address of Hochschule Bremen; its domain also determines the role. There is no role selection.
steps: Step 1: first name, last name, private email address as the login name, university address and password. The password is at least twelve characters long.
Steps 2 and 3: one six-digit code each, one sent to the private address and one to the university address.
You always sign in with the private address, never with the university address.
“Forgot password” on the sign-in page sends a six-digit code to the private address; with that code and a new password the account can be opened again.
account.imageAlt: The first step of registration: a card with progress dots and the fields for first name, last name, private email address, university address and password.

appearance.title: Language, light and dark
appearance.text: On the right of the header sit the controls that belong to presentation: the question mark leads to this page, DE or EN switches the language, the moon or sun icon switches between light and dark mode.
steps: Language and mode stay in the same place at every window width. On narrow screens the question mark moves into the menu behind the three lines, because exactly one menu leads there.
Light or dark mode is remembered by the browser and still applies on your next visit.
The language choice is not stored: after a reload the interface is back in German.
A second way to this page sits in the footer, under “Platform”.
appearance.imageAlt: The full-width header: on the left the Hochschule Bremen wordmark with the addition E-Portfolio, in the middle the navigation entries, on the right the question mark, the language code, the mode switch and the sign-in button.
appearance.imageCaption: The header, here without being signed in.

contact.title: Asking questions and reporting problems
contact.text: “Contact & support” accepts enquiries, deliberately also without signing in: the most common case is that someone cannot get in, and a form behind the sign-in does not help there.
steps: Name, email address, category, subject and description are all required. A signed-in account finds name and address filled in, which does not make them optional.
The enquiry arrives in the administration area; the reply comes by email.
contact.imageAlt: The public contact form with the fields name, email address, category, subject and description as well as the send button.

students.title: Your portfolio and the editor
students.intro: Every signed-in account keeps a portfolio of its own and can create, write and submit projects for review.

myPortfolio.title: My portfolio
myPortfolio.text: “My portfolio” lists all of your own work regardless of its state, next to your own profile card.
steps: The bar above the cards filters by state: all, draft, submitted, approved, published, revision.

The pencil opens the editor while the work is in draft or revision. The bin only appears on your own drafts: deleting is done by the author alone and only in draft. Anyone involved as a project member leaves the project instead.
“New project” immediately creates a draft and opens it. Until it has a title it carries a placeholder.

“Edit profile” changes name, picture, short introduction (500 characters at most) and the password. Changing the private address additionally requires the current password and a code sent to the new address; until that is confirmed the old address remains the login name.
myPortfolio.imageAlt: The page “My portfolio”: a heading with the button “New project”, below it the state filter and your own project cards with pencil and bin; on the right the profile card with initials, name, role badge, private address and the button “Edit profile”.

metadata.title: Details of a project
metadata.text: Besides its content, every work carries details that determine how it is found and who is responsible for it. They live in the metadata form, reachable from the editor through “Edit metadata”.
steps: Seven details are required as soon as you submit: project type, faculty, degree programme, degree, category, semester and the responsible editor.
Project members are added through the person search; the function label beside them is optional.
The project side chooses the responsible editor itself, that is the author and the project members, while the work is in draft or revision. From submission onwards only the administration assigns.
Anyone who belongs to the project side is not offered for selection: nobody takes on their own work editorially.
Tags are free text, are created when you save and are limited to five per work.
metadata.imageAlt: The metadata form of a project with a cover image area, title, summary and the select fields for project type, faculty, degree programme, degree, category and semester.
metadata.imageCaption: The metadata form of a draft.

workspace.title: The writing surface
workspace.text: The editor opens through the pencil on a card. The toolbar sits at the top, the content in the middle with cover image, title and summary, and the details of the project on the right.
steps: Editing is only possible in the states draft and revision. In any other state the surface is read-only and a message names the reason.

Only one person edits at a time. The lock covers every writing view of the work, including the metadata form: whoever has the metadata open also holds the editor. If someone else has the work open, the page says so with their name and the time.
Saving happens on its own, a little over a second after the last keystroke. The state is shown in the header.
“Preview” shows the work in its public view, “Print as PDF” produces the print version, and the button beside them inserts a table of contents or brings it up to date.
workspace.imageAlt: The writing surface of the editor: at the top the toolbar with back, undo, redo and the formatting controls, below it cover image, title and the content; on the right the column with state, history and the project details.

blocks.title: Inserting and moving blocks
blocks.text: A contribution consists of blocks. There are two ways to insert one, both offering the same choice: the plus sign to the left of a block, and the slash at the beginning of an empty line.
steps: Ten block types: image, gallery, video, audio, document, embed, formula, table, source code and divider.
Headings, paragraphs, lists and quotes are not created here but through the toolbar at the top; the table of contents through its own button in the header.
Blocks are moved with the handle beside them; by keyboard through Alt+F9, then the arrow keys, Enter drops the block and Escape puts it back.
A deleted block comes back in full with “Undo”, which is why deleting a block does not ask first.
blocks.imageAlt: The editor with the insert bar open: a pill of eleven round buttons sits above the content, on the left the close cross, beside it the icons for image, gallery, video, audio, document, embed, formula, table, source code and divider.
blocks.imageCaption: The insert bar at the plus sign; the slash offers the same choice.

formatting.title: Formatting text
formatting.text: The toolbar stays in the header at all times and acts on the current selection in the text.
steps: On the left the block type menu: text and heading levels 1 to 6.
Then bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, inline code, superscript, subscript and the link.
Then bulleted list, numbered list, quote and alignment. Justified is blocked on a heading.
On the right text colour and highlight. The editor only ever applies one of the two: the second replaces the first. “Default” removes the formatting.
Alt+F10 moves the keyboard focus into the toolbar, Escape returns to the text.
formatting.imageAlt: The header of the editor with the toolbar: back, undo, redo, the block type menu showing “Heading 1”, the character formats, lists, quote, alignment, text colour and highlight, and on the right “Preview” and “Submit”.
formatting.imageCaption: The toolbar in the editor header.

sidebar.title: State, history, details and comments
sidebar.text: Beside the writing surface sit the current state of the work, its history and two collapsible sections.
steps: “History” lists every change of state with its time and the person, newest first.
“Project information” summarises the details and leads into the form through “Edit metadata”.
“Comments” shows the change requests from the editorial side and accepts replies. Internal editorial notes do not appear there.
sidebar.imageAlt: The editor sidebar: at the top the state badge “Draft” and the button “History”, below it the expanded section “Project information” with project type, faculty, degree programme, degree, semester, category, subject, project members, editors and tags, and at the bottom the collapsed section “Comments”.

workflow.title: Submitting, withdrawing, revising
workflow.text: A work passes through five states. What is possible at any moment depends on which one it is in.
steps: Draft: editable and visible to the project side and the administration. “Submit” first leads to the metadata, because seven details are required there.
Submitted: no longer editable. “Withdraw” takes the work back to draft after a confirmation.
Revision: editable again. The editorial side has left change requests; you can only submit again once none of them is open. The project side marks them resolved itself, in the comment column.
Approved: cleared on the merits, but not public yet.
Published: visible to everyone, including people who are not signed in.

editors.title: Editorial work: review, comment, release
editors.intro: Editors review the works assigned to them and decide whether to release them. An account with the administrator role may do the same, even without an assignment.

list.title: My reviews
list.text: “My reviews” lists exactly those works for which you are entered as the editor. Drafts never appear there: a work becomes visible only when it is submitted.
steps: Four counters at the top: submitted, approved, published, revision.
Below them the search field and three filters for degree programme, semester and subject, plus the state bar.
In the table the menu at the end of a row leads to “Review”, “Nominate for top 10” and “Give up assignment”.
list.imageAlt: The page “My reviews”: four counter tiles for submitted, approved, published and revision, below them search field and filters, then the table with the columns project, students, degree programme, semester, subject and status.

open.title: Reviewing a work
open.text: “Review” opens the work in review mode: on the left the content as readers see it, on the right the editorial column.
steps: The switch at the top toggles between preview and review.
Below it sit the state badge and the “History” button with every change so far.
The content itself is not edited here; feedback goes through the comments.
open.imageAlt: Review mode of a submitted work: on the left cover image, title and content, on the right the switch between preview and review, the state badge “Submitted”, “History” and the comment column.
open.imageCaption: Review mode of a submitted work.

comments.title: Notes, change requests and replies
comments.text: The comment column knows three kinds, and they differ not in appearance but in effect.
steps: Reply: visible to everyone who may read the work. On a published work the comment list is therefore retrievable without signing in as well.
Note: for the editorial side and the administration only. It is not delivered to the project side at all.
Change request: also visible to everyone with read access, carrying the state “Open” or “Resolved”. The project side marks it resolved. While one is open the work cannot be submitted again.
Enter sends, Shift and Enter make a line break.
comments.imageAlt: The comment column of a work: a note on a yellow background with its author, the marking NOTE and a timestamp, below it the three buttons reply, note and change request as well as the input field with a character counter.
comments.imageCaption: The comment column in review mode.

decide.title: Approving, publishing, sending back
decide.text: The decision is made through the menu on the state badge. Whatever is not possible right now stays visible and carries its reason; nothing disappears silently.
steps: Approve: the work counts as cleared on the merits, but it is not public yet.

Publish: the work is visible to everyone, including people who are not signed in. After that it can only be taken back through “Request revision”, and only once it is no longer in the top 10 list; while it is held there the server rejects the step.
Request revision: a reason is required. It appears as a change request in the project side's editor.

Back to review: only out of revision, and only by the assigned editor or the administration. The same conditions as for submitting apply, that is no open change request and the seven required details.
Every one of these steps asks first and names the title of the work.
decide.imageAlt: Review mode with the menu on the state badge open: the possible targets sit below one another, impossible ones are dimmed and carry a line of reasoning.
decide.imageCaption: The menu for changing the state.

fourEyes.title: Four eyes: nobody releases their own work
fourEyes.text: Approve and publish are blocked as soon as you belong to the project side yourself, that is as author or project member. This holds even when the work is assigned to you editorially, and it holds for every role including administration.
steps: Sending a work back for revision is not affected.
The block follows current membership, not history: leaving the project members releases you from it, but you are then no longer named as a contributor either.
Giving up your own assignment as the last assigned editor sends the work back to draft. That is only possible while the work is submitted or in revision.

nominate.title: Proposing a work for the top 10
nominate.text: Published works can be proposed for the top 10 list on the home page. The administration decides on inclusion.
steps: You propose through the menu in the “My reviews” table, choosing a tier: place 1, places 2 to 5, or places 6 to 10. The tier is an assessment, not a promise of a place.
At most one proposal is open per work, and a work that is already in the list cannot be proposed again.
Your own proposals are listed on the same page and can be filtered by state: open, accepted, rejected, withdrawn.
An open proposal can be withdrawn.

admins.title: Administration area
admins.intro: The administration area gathers everything that concerns the platform as a whole. It is reachable through the entry “Administration” in the header.

dashboard.title: Dashboard and section navigation
dashboard.text: The entry point shows where work is waiting: the number of works per state, the user statistics by role and account state, and the number of open top 10 proposals.
steps: The section navigation on the left holds nine entries, from dashboard to home page texts.
The entry “Support” carries the number of open enquiries, so it is visible without a click.
dashboard.imageAlt: The dashboard of the administration area: on the left the section navigation with dashboard, projects, top 10, users, categories, semesters, study structure, support and home page texts, on the right tiles with the number of all projects per state and below them the user statistics as ring charts.
dashboard.imageCaption: The entry point of the administration area.

projects.title: Managing all projects
projects.text: The only view that also lists other people's drafts. It filters across all states and allows interventions nobody else has.
steps: Select several rows and publish them together or send them back for revision.
Assign the responsible editor, also after the fact.
Delete a work. That cannot be undone, which is why it asks first.
projects.imageAlt: Project management in the administration area: search field and filters above a table with checkboxes, title, author, faculty, state and last change.

users.title: Accounts and roles
users.text: Create accounts, change roles, deactivate accounts and reset passwords. The role of an account can be changed here and only here.
steps: The role determines the rights: students write, editors review, administrators manage and may additionally do both.
A deactivated account can no longer sign in.
A reset password forces a change at the next sign-in.
users.imageAlt: User management: search field and filters above a table with name, address, role, account state and a menu per row, and at the top right the button for creating an account.

masterData.title: Master data: categories, semesters, study structure
masterData.text: These three lists feed the select fields in the metadata form and the filter groups in the project library. What is not listed here cannot be chosen there.
steps: Study structure: faculties, degree programmes and modules, hierarchically in three columns.
Categories can be merged when two of them mean the same thing; the works concerned move along.
Semesters carry an active switch and an order of their own.
Anything a work still refers to cannot be deleted. The active switch is there for that case: it removes the entry from the select fields without touching the existing data.
masterData.imageAlt: The study structure in the administration area: three columns side by side for faculties, degree programmes and modules, each with its own list and its own button for adding an entry.
masterData.imageCaption: The study structure as an example of master data.

top10.title: Curating the top 10
top10.text: This is where it is decided which works appear on the home page and in which order.
steps: Accept or reject the proposals from the editorial side.
Ten places, reorderable; every change takes effect immediately.
The change log records who changed what and when.
top10.imageAlt: Top 10 management: on the left the ten places with the works filling them and arrows for reordering, beside them the open editorial proposals with their tier and the decision.

support.title: Support enquiries
support.text: The enquiries from the public contact form arrive here, with category, sender and state.
steps: Three states: open, in progress, resolved.
Replies go by email; afterwards the entry can be closed or deleted.
support.imageAlt: Management of support enquiries: filters by state and category above a list of enquiries with subject, sender, category, time and state.

siteContent.title: Home page texts
siteContent.text: Fifteen pieces of text on the public home page can be maintained here, separately per language.
steps: The opening section with its overline, two heading lines, introduction and the call to action leading to the top 10 list, which makes five places.
Overline, heading and explanation above the top 10 list, which makes three.
The closing section with overline, heading, text, the three figure labels and the link into the project library, which makes seven.
Anything left empty here falls back to the text shipped with the application.
All other texts of the application cannot be maintained editorially, this help page included.
siteContent.imageAlt: The maintenance form for the home page texts: input fields listed one below the other per piece of text, each separated into a German and an English version.
